original_question: Let I be an ideal of a Jordan pair V, let can: V -> V/I be the canonical map, and let PE(V, I) be the kernel of the induced surjective homomorphism PE(can): PE(V) -> PE(V/I). Describe the group PE(V, I) by explicit generators and relations.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 on the relative projective elementary group of a Jordan pair: for an ideal I of a Jordan pair V, describe the kernel PE(V,I)=ker(PE(can):PE(V)→PE(V/I)) by an explicit presentation. This is the formulation flagged at the start of the chapter and then situated by Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right object and the right level of specificity: it uses an ideal I◁V, the canonical quotient map can:V→V/I, the induced surjection on projective elementary groups, and the kernel PE(V,I). That is exactly the relative projective elementary group whose explicit presentation is the paper’s opening problem/conjectural target. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))
missing_details: State that V is a Jordan pair V=(V+,V−), and I=(I+,I−) is an ideal of V; otherwise the plus/minus structure is implicit rather than stand-alone. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

Use the paper’s name for the object, namely the relative projective elementary group PE(V,I), not just 'the kernel'. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

Specify the ambient algebraic setting used throughout the chapter/book: Jordan pairs in the Loos/Neher sense, i.e. the quadratic Jordan-pair framework over a commutative base ring with 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))

Make clear that the request is for an intrinsic generators-and-relations presentation attached to the pair (V,I), not merely a subgroup description inside PE(V). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

Indicate that this is the paper’s conjectural/open formulation in §1, with Proposition 1.2 giving nearby sharpening/reformulation and Theorem 1.3 providing the initial positive evidence in a special case. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

Spell out that PE(can) is induced by the quotient morphism of Jordan pairs can:V→V/I and is surjective; your draft uses this correctly but leaves it implicit as background. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))
refined_question: Let V=(V+,V−) be a Jordan pair over the base ring used in the paper, let I=(I+,I−)◁V be an ideal, let can:V→V/I be the canonical quotient morphism, and define the relative projective elementary group by PE(V,I):=ker(PE(can):PE(V)→PE(V/I)). Find an explicit, intrinsic presentation of PE(V,I) by generators and defining relations. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))
justification: The draft is already narrowly aimed at the chapter’s opening relative-group problem: it singles out the kernel of the quotient map on projective elementary groups, which is the exact object denoted PE(V,I) in the paper’s introductory setup. The only real gaps are stand-alone notation, the official name 'relative projective elementary group', and the ambient Jordan-pair assumptions. Keeping the question at the level of an explicit presentation by generators and relations stays closest to the paper’s intent and avoids broadening it beyond Conjecture 1.1 and its immediate introductory context. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))
